subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 50
source.subtopic: Multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 and 5 (weeks 3-10; to 40 in weeks 3-4)

show.line: Three bicycles. Each has two wheels. Two, four, six. Three groups of two is six. Three times two equals six!

rounds.prompt: Four pairs of shoes. Count the shoes in twos. How many shoes?
rounds.praise: Eight shoes! Four times two is eight.

rounds.prompt: Three hands. Five fingers on each. Count in fives. How many fingers?
rounds.praise: Fifteen! Three times five is fifteen.

rounds.prompt: Five times two. Five groups of two. Say the answer.
Six times five. Count in fives six times. What is the answer?
rounds.praise: Thirty! Five, ten, fifteen, twenty, twenty-five, thirty.

rounds.story: Mama buys four packets of sweets. Each packet has five sweets. How many sweets in all?
rounds.praise: Twenty! Four times five is twenty.

rounds.prompt: Which picture shows three times two?
rounds.praise: Yes! Three groups with two in each.

rounds.prompt: Seven times two. What is the answer?
rounds.praise: Fourteen! Seven times two is fourteen.

hints: Count in twos or fives, once for each group.
Times means groups of. Three times two is three groups of two.

beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Five, ten, fifteen. Four times five is fifteen!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! I only counted three fives. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's count four fives together. Five, ten, fifteen, twenty!

parent_line: Can work out groups of two and groups of five up to 10 groups.
